items.name: createShortcutGroup
items.summary: Creates an imperative group controller for many shortcut registrations.
items.returns: A `ShortcutGroup` that can add and unbind multiple shortcuts together
examples:
```ts
const group = createShortcutGroup()
group.add($.mod.key("s").on(onSave))
group.add($.key("escape").on(onClose))
group.unbindAll()
```

items.name: detectPlatform
items.summary:
Detect the current OS platform for modifier normalization and display formatting.
Result is memoized for the page lifecycle.

items.name: ExceptPredicate
items.summary: Custom predicate for excluding shortcuts in certain conditions
items.returns: `true` to skip the shortcut, `false` to allow it

items.name: ExceptPreset
items.summary:
Built-in exception presets for common scenarios
- "input" - Skip when focused on input, textarea, or select
- "editable" - Skip when focused on contentEditable elements
- "typing" - Skip in any text input context (combines input + editable)
- "modal" - Skip when a modal/dialog is open (checks [data-modal] or [role="dialog"])
- "disabled" - Skip when focused element is disabled

items.name: formatShortcut
items.summary: Format a shortcut string for display with platform-aware symbols
items.returns: Formatted display string (e.g., "⌘S" on Mac, "Ctrl+S" on Windows)
examples:
```ts
formatShortcut("cmd+s") // "⌘S" on Mac, "Ctrl+S" on Windows
formatShortcut("ctrl+shift+p", "mac") // "⌃⇧P"
```

items.name: registerShortcutMap
items.summary:
Registers an object-based shortcut map in one call and returns per-action handles.

`keys` accepts one combo (`"mod+s"`), one sequence (`"g then d"`), or an
array of alternatives (`["escape", "mod+d"]`) where any alternative fires
the handler. Each alternative may itself be a sequence string.
items.signature: <T extends ShortcutMap>(builder: ShortcutBuilder, shortcutMap: T): ShortcutMapResult<T>

params.name: shortcutMap
params.description: - Record of action ids to key bindings, handlers, and options

items.returns: A result map with one `ShortcutResult` per shortcut id

items.name: useShortcut
items.summary: React hook for registering chainable keyboard shortcuts

items.name: useShortcutBinding
items.summary: React hook for one cleanup-safe shortcut binding.
items.signature: (keys: string | string[], handler: ShortcutHandler, options?: HandlerOptions, shortcutOptions?: UseShortcutOptions): ShortcutResult

params.name: keys
params.description: - Shortcut combo string, sequence string, or array of alternative combos, such as `"mod+s"`, `"g then d"`, or `["escape", "mod+d"]`

params.name: handler
params.description: - Handler invoked when the shortcut matches

items.returns: A stable `ShortcutResult` handle. Before the effect runs, the handle is disabled and uses the provided keys as its display text.
examples:
```ts
const closeShortcut = useShortcutBinding({
  keys: ["escape", "mod+d"],
  handler: closeDialog,
  options: { description: "Close dialog" },
})
```

items.name: useShortcutGroup
items.summary: React hook that returns a stable `ShortcutGroup` instance.
items.returns: A memoized `ShortcutGroup` tied to the component lifecycle

items.name: useShortcutMap
items.summary:
React hook that registers a shortcut map and automatically unbinds on cleanup.

Handlers are kept in a ref, so inline handler functions never cause
re-registration. The returned map and its per-id results are stable object
references, safe to destructure at any point in the component lifecycle.
items.signature: <T extends ShortcutMap>(shortcutMap: T, options?: UseShortcutOptions): ShortcutMapResult<T>

params.name: shortcutMap
params.description: - Record of action ids to key bindings, handlers, and options

items.returns: A map of `ShortcutResult` keyed by your shortcut ids

items.name: UseShortcutOptions
items.summary: Options for the `useShortcut` hook
